itineraries.title: 48 Hours in Austin, Texas
itineraries.summary: A structured weekend itinerary for a first-time Austin trip on the creator's own site (last updated January 22, 2026): Friday 2pm downtown bike ride (B-Cycle Weekender Pass $19.49, Lady Bird Lake, Zilker Park, Doug Sahm Hill skyline views), food trucks, a 5pm South Congress stroll, the 7-8pm Congress Avenue Bridge bat flight, and 9pm Rainey Street bar-hopping; Saturday brunch at 24 Diner, Hope Outdoor Gallery street art, Torchy's Tacos, a free Texas State Capitol tour, Franklin's BBQ dinner, sunset drinks at Azul Rooftop, live music at the Continental Club, and the Midnight Cowboy speakeasy; Sunday breakfast tacos.

itineraries.title: How to Spend a Weekend in Tupelo, Mississippi: A Travel Guide
itineraries.summary: A structured 3-day Tupelo weekend on the creator's own site (updated ~mid-August 2026): Day 1 downtown Tupelo (murals and the It's Electric Neon Lights Trail, shopping at MLM Clothiers/Bolt/Reed's, Caron Gallery and GumTree Museum of Art, Lost + Found Coffee Co., Queen's Reward Meadery tasting, dinner at Stables Downtown Grill); Day 2 Elvis footsteps (Talbot House Bakery & Cafe, Elvis Presley Birthplace, Johnnie's Drive-In, Elvis' Tupelo Driving Tour, Tupelo Hardware Company, Forklift dinner, Blue Canoe live music); Day 3 Natchez Trace Parkway Visitor Center, Chickasaw Village Site, Tombigbee State Park, Oren Dunn City Museum, and Crave Tupelo dessert bar.

items.name: Hotel Tupelo
items.description: Boutique hotel in downtown Tupelo close to restaurants, shops and live music; alternative: Holiday Inn & Suites Tupelo North

items.name: Downtown Tupelo murals and It's Electric Neon Lights Trail
items.description: Day 1: explore downtown murals and neon installations; the guide recommends downloading the It's Electric: Neon Lights Trail for public art after dark

items.name: Downtown shopping: MLM Clothiers, Bolt, Reed's
items.description: Day 1: MLM Clothiers (one of Mississippi's oldest menswear stores), Bolt (rock-and-roll aesthetic boutique), Reed's (Tupelo institution since 1905) and Reed's GumTree Bookstore

items.name: Caron Gallery and GumTree Museum of Art
items.description: Day 1: browse contemporary Southern artists at the Caron Gallery, then the GumTree Museum of Art (showcasing regional artists for 40+ years)

items.name: Lost + Found Coffee Co.
items.description: Day 1 caffeine break: specialty roastery; the guide orders a cereal milk latte or pour-over with a pastry

items.name: Queen's Reward Meadery tasting
items.description: Day 1: Mississippi's first and only meadery - guided tasting flights, mead-and-cheese pairings and mead slushie flights from the female-owned, small-batch producer

items.name: Stables Downtown Grill
items.description: Day 1 dinner: blackened catfish nachos and Southern classics; the alley patio is one of Tupelo's best outdoor dining spots

items.name: Talbot House Bakery & Cafe
items.description: Day 2 breakfast: house-made pastries, cinnamon rolls in various flavors and enormous chocolate chip cookies

items.name: Elvis Presley Birthplace
items.description: Day 2: the modest two-room shotgun house built by Vernon Presley, plus the museum, the Assembly of God church where Elvis discovered gospel music, memorial gardens, the Becoming sculpture and the Reflections area

items.name: Johnnie's Drive-In
items.description: Day 2 lunch: the cash-only diner serving Tupelo since 1945 where Elvis was a regular - order a doughburger and ask for the famous Elvis booth

items.name: Elvis' Tupelo Driving Tour
items.description: Day 2 afternoon: the driving tour past the original Reed's Department Store, Elvis' schools and the historic Shake Rag neighborhood

items.name: Tupelo Hardware Company
items.description: Day 2: the store where an 11-year-old Elvis arrived hoping for a bicycle and left with a $7.75 guitar; being preserved as an interpretive attraction

items.name: Forklift
items.description: Day 2 dinner: elevated Southern cuisine with creative cocktails and seasonal menus; patio tables on warm evenings

items.name: Blue Canoe live music
items.description: Day 2 late night: Southern comfort food, craft beer and live music at Blue Canoe; its Cathead Stage hosted Chris Stapleton, Jason Isbell and others pre-fame

items.name: Natchez Trace Parkway Visitor Center (milepost 266)
items.description: Day 3: start at the Parkway Visitor Center at milepost 266 for exhibits and ranger trail recommendations along the 444-mile scenic route

items.name: Chickasaw Village Site
items.description: Day 3: short interpretive trail through the former Chickasaw village site with exhibits on Chickasaw life and culture

items.name: Tombigbee State Park
items.description: Day 3 outdoor excursion: the park around Lake Lee offers hiking, fishing, paddling and disc golf, plus cabins and campsites

items.name: Oren Dunn City Museum at Ballard Park
items.description: Day 3: restored dairy barn museum tracing Tupelo's history through its people, industries and events; caboose and relics for photos

items.name: Crave Tupelo dessert bar
items.description: Day 3 finale: downtown dessert bar known for over-the-top sweets; opens evenings on Sundays
